newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Up to six said killed in Somalia aid convoy clash.
newsitem.headline: Up to six said killed in Somalia aid convoy clash.

text.p: Up to six people were killed in a clash in the southwestern Somali city of Baidoa between militiamen and gunmen escorting a food convoy, a survivor said on Saturday.
One of the wounded, evacuated to a south Mogadishu hospital, told reporters fighting broke out on Friday between the convoy's escorts and militiamen loyal to faction leader Hussein Aideed in Baidoa.

He said shooting started after the local commander in Baidoa refused to allow the convoy loaded with food destined for the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) through on its way to Bardera town, saying only his own men could escort it.
In Nairobi, an ICRC spokesman said: "Something happened around Baidoa. There was some shooting, there were some deaths. We hear either two or five. But it is not clear what exactly happened."

He said the convoy was carrying food destined for the ICRC but it was not strictly an ICRC food convoy because the agency contracted Somali businessmen to transport food in Somalia in unmarked trucks. No ICRC staff were with the convoy, he added.

Some other foreign agencies have demanded Somalia's rival faction chiefs provide security before they can even envisage responding to the leaders' calls for large amounts of food and staff to be dispatched to drought-stricken areas of Somalia.
Some 300,000 people were killed in a famine fuelled by civil war in Somalia in 1992 before U.S. and U.N. troops intervened to protect agency convoys and supplies against marauding gunmen.
